quotes.name: Cedric Nakamura
quotes.quote: From behind the counter, you see two different crowds. The folks walking past on Telegraph are mostly new — younger, on their phones, heading to the tech offices or the pop-ups. The ones who actually come in are the regulars, the ones who've been here since before the rent signs went up. We get a few curious walk-ins, sure, but the people who buy records are the same faces I've seen for years. The block's moving faster than the store is, if that makes sense.

quotes.quote: Things have picked up some, sure. The lunch rush gets longer, and the coffee machine doesn't stop. But I'm in the back, elbow-deep in suds. It pays the bills, and that's what matters.

quotes.name: Derek Obi
quotes.quote: I work at Oakland Tech Collective, so I'm on the side that feels the block moving. The building's got new people coming in all the time, and there's a hum to it. But when I walk past Art Walk Cafe or Night Walk Records, I see the same folks, the same pace. They're not standing still, but it's a different rhythm. I think the tech places bring a certain energy, but the small spots—they're the ones that make the block feel like a neighborhood. You watch them, and you wonder if they feel the same push we do, or if they're just holding on.
